Overlay Board

Upload a data file or program PDF. Overlay Board lays out the whole card: past performances, scratches, money moves, and where the board likes a horse.

1 Bring in your data

Brisnet data file

Brisnet’s Single File export, or a multi-part card (the four-file .DRF/.DR2/.DR3/.DR4 set some tracks ship). A .zip is fine and is opened for you — for a multi-part card send the whole zip, since the four files only work as a set. If .drf looks greyed out in the picker, rename it to .csv; the parser reads the contents, not the name.

Program PDF

Brisnet-style past-performance sheet. Runs in the browser; if it hangs on a phone, use Paste text instead.

Apply scratches from the Equibase feed

Load the data file above first, then choose the track’s Changes & Scratches feed or paste it below. Scratches are ticked automatically by race and program number. Rider changes are flagged on the card, with the new rider’s meet record where the file has one.

ML odds comes in with the file. Final starts empty — fill it in at the track; it never overwrites the morning line. Surface fit and Class are optional. Tick Scr for a scratch and rebuild the card: scratched horses drop out and the field renormalizes.

▦ Decision board

The whole card at a glance, then each race in full underneath. Two separate lines name a horse, and this is the only place the tool does so. Figure favourite — the market favourite also holds the field's single highest average of its last three speed figures. Price play — a separate line, used only where a figure favourite is not available: the morning-line favourite is second in the field on career earnings per start.

🖨 Printable page

The whole card on one page — Decision board, race cards and full field. Tap the button to print or save it as a PDF; your browser's own Share also works from here.

? How to read this

Using the board — what to bet, what to read

Race plans. Every race is PLAY — WIN BET + EXACTAS, EXACTAS ONLY — NO WIN BET, or SKIP. The tier line under each plan refers to the win bet only. SKIP: the field is too lightly raced to read, it has 9 or more runners and no figure favourite, or it is a maiden race with 2 or more first-time starters. PLAY: the Key is the top-ranked horse and Use lists the next three (next four in a field of 9 or more) — the horses to build exotics around, with two ready tickets: the Key on top of the Use horses, or a box of the four. A win bet is shown only where a BET verdict applies, with its condition.

Today’s verdicts. Every race gets one verdict at the top of the Decision board and on its card. BET — DEFINITIVE (the figure favourite meets every definitive condition): win, plus an exacta with it on top of the next four ranked. BET — CONDITIONAL (a figure favourite with no flag that misses one definitive condition): a conditional win wager — only if the horse is 2-1 or higher at post. Enter it with that condition and the odds at the off decide. EXOTICS (top-ranked horse with no ⬇ flag or ⊖ fade, 8 or fewer runners, race not red): exacta with it on top of the next three ranked, no win bet. PASS: no bet, with the reason.

Every race lands in one of four situations. Work down the Decision board and treat each one this way.

1. BET — DEFINITIVE. The figure favourite also has the top last figure on its own, has been in the money in most of its recent starts, and shows early speed (2 or more speed points), with no claiming drop or surface switch against it. Every condition points the same way: win, plus the exacta key.

2. BET — CONDITIONAL. The favourite holds the top 3-race average on its own with no flag, but misses one definitive condition (the top last figure, recent form or early speed). Win as a conditional wager, only at 2-1 or higher at post. Check the MAIN THREAT line and the Top 4 for the horse most likely to beat it.

3. FIGURE FAV, PASS-flagged — look hard at the Main Threat. The favourite tops the figures but is entered well below its recent claiming level or switches surface from its last start. That flag names a real weakness today, so this is the situation where the MAIN THREAT deserves the most attention — read its figures, Prime Power and speed facts beside the favourite's before deciding.

4. NO FIGURE FAV — read the field. The favourite does not hold the top 3-race average on its own (or there are no morning lines). The card shows the top-ranked horse and the NEXT RANKED line. Look for the horse that leads the field on the 3-race average while also high on Prime Power and near the top of the betting.

When the Main Threat matters least. When the figure favourite is BET — DEFINITIVE, and above all a CLEAR FIGURE FAV, read the Main Threat as the horse to run second, not as a reason to change the call.

Top 4 — which of the four the record backs. Each Top 4 horse shows the facts it leads the other three on (last figure, 3-race average, Prime Power, early speed, recent form). The more of the five it leads, the more the past performances support it; a horse that leads on none of them is the first one to cross off.

⬇ Demotion flags. Two facts push a horse down the ranking: FIGURE FROM OTHER SURFACE — its top last figure was run on a different surface from today's — and TROUBLE LAST OUT — it finished 4th or worse last time with a trouble comment (steadied, bumped, checked, stumbled). The horses behind it move up; pretenders stay out of the ranking.

⊖ Fade signals. Five facts that mark a horse down: back within 14 days; stretching out from a sprint to a route; first blinkers on a horse with 4 or fewer starts; a trainer winning under 10% in this horse's situation (from the file's trainer statistics), unless the horse finished ahead of a rival in today's field within the last 90 days; the best closer in a dirt sprint. Each one is noted on the horse and adds 5 to its rank score. One signal: use the horse underneath, not on top. Two or more: strike it.

Below the Top 4. The 5th-ranked horse is a reasonable extra name for exotics. Horses ranked 7th or lower can be passed over.

PRICE PLAY and the Concurrence fold — information only. The Price Play names the favourite from the earnings line in races with no figure favourite; read it, don't bet it. The Concurrence fold shows whether two other selection methods agree; agreement alone does not make a stronger bet.

In one line: follow the verdicts — BET — DEFINITIVE and BET — CONDITIONAL to win, EXOTICS as exactas only, check the Main Threat when the favourite is flagged, and use the Top 4 leads to decide who belongs in your exotics.

The figure favourite frozen rule

Only the morning-line favourite is ever eligible — nobody else can be named. It becomes the figure favourite under one condition: it also holds the field's sole highest mean of its last three speed figures. A tie at the top doesn't count. Second on that figure doesn't count. Needs three runners in the race carrying a figure at all.

That's the whole rule. Nothing about readability, pace, works, or barn entries touches it — those all sit next to the figure favourite as information, never as a gate.

Price play fallback rule

Used only when no figure favourite fires: the morning-line favourite is second in the field on career earnings per start. A separate, weaker line — logged, never treated the same as a figure favourite.

Contenders / Questionable / Pretenders

Every runner sorted into one of three buckets based on price and form evidence. Contenders are live. Questionable horses lack clean evidence either way. Pretenders are priced out with nothing to rescue them. This is what "Also with a shot" and Top 4 both draw from.

Top 4 probable

The four highest-ranked Contenders by figure, shown per race and in their own tab for a quick scan across the whole card. Tap any name to open its full past performances; tap the name again inside that view to come straight back to Top 4.

Also with a shot

The rest of the field, ordered by the same read that flagged Army's Marauder — competitive-at-today's-level ratio first, earnings per start as the tiebreaker. Not by price. A horse with no comparable starts to judge sorts to the end, not the top.

Worth a second look — pace display only

Fires when the figure favourite's own last three starts show a fading majority (2 of 3, read from the pace figures below) and a genuine Contender in the same field shows the opposite. Doesn't change the figure favourite.

When the two methods disagree

If AI(1) and AI(2) rank different horses first, the race is labelled: TWO-HORSE RACE (7 or fewer runners and AI(2)'s horse is AI(1)'s #2 — one of the two usually wins); SMALL FIELD, SPLIT (8 or fewer, not a maiden, AI(2)'s horse in AI(1)'s top 3 — use both on top, with the next horse); WIDE OPEN (9 or more runners, or a maiden race — a third horse usually wins); otherwise SPLIT.

Tiers and percentages

Each race shows a tier for its named horse and the share of such horses that won on the cards in the pack: Tier 1 DEFINITIVE in a FOCUS race with a clear #1 (75%) · Tier 2 DEFINITIVE (64%) · Tier 3 SOLID PICK (58%) · Tier 4 CONDITIONAL, when 2-1 or higher at post (53%) · Tier 5 top pick in a FOCUS race (39%) · Tier 6 top pick in a CONSIDER race (23%) · Tier 7 top pick in a LOW race (22%). Tiers 1-3 are bets, Tier 4 only at 2-1 or higher; Tiers 5-7 carry no win-bet edge and say so. These are past results on the pack's cards, which the rules were built from; on new cards expect them to run a few points lower. When you record winners on the race cards, the percentages blend in your own results, and the scorecard at the top of the board shows how each tier, bet type and confidence level is doing.

BET — SOLID PICK

A win bet on the top-ranked horse when neither DEFINITIVE nor CONDITIONAL applies, and either (A) its morning line is 8-5 or shorter, it has the best Prime Power in the field, at most one no-finish trip comment in its last four, and the race is not low priority; or (B) its morning line is 2-1 or shorter, the field has 8 or fewer runners, it has the best last figure in the field, and its case tally is +4 or better.

Strong challengers

The tier line names any strong challenger: a contender that beats the top-ranked horse on two or more of Prime Power, last figure and early speed. Their edges are in Race Facts under EDGES OVER #1.

Ability and fair odds

FAIR (DATA) is the price each horse's own record would justify, worked out from the past performances alone, with no odds of any kind: its 3-race, last and best figures against the best in today's field, its Prime Power against the best, its early-speed points, how often it was in the money in its last four starts, whether it won last time, any ⬇ flags or ⊖ fades, and whether it is a first-time starter. ABILITY is the horse's rank in the field on those same fair odds — #1 has the strongest record. Under FAIR, ML shorter means the morning line rates the horse better than its record does; ML longer means the record rates it better than the morning line.

Concurrence — AI(1) / AI(2)

AI(1) is the top horse in this board's ranking. AI(2) is the top horse in a second, independent ranking ported into this file and run on the same field and scratches; it weighs recent figures, form, pace, surface and class and does not use the morning line. CONCURRENT: both put the same horse first. DIFFERENT: they disagree. A figure favourite that AI(2) does not rank first is not bet. Agreement is shown as information; it is not a bet on its own.

Readability display only

How thick the field's data actually is — green, yellow (thin), or red (blind). Never suppresses or overrides the figure favourite. A blind-record figure favourite still fires; the color just tells you how much you're trusting a thin field when it does.

"Too close to call" display only

Flags when the top few horses are within 3 points of each other on Prime Power — a different rating from the speed figure the figure favourite uses, so this can fire even when the figure favourite's own figure has a clean, sole leader. It describes the field; it doesn't change the figure favourite.

Reading a past-performance line

Date, track, distance, surface, post, class move (▲ tougher · = about the same · ▼ easier than today), finish, who won/placed/showed, the BRIS speed figure, Pace, class text, trip comment.

Pace shows the BRIS pace-call figures for that race in order (2-call, 4-call, 6-call, 8-call, late pace — same rating scale as Speed) plus a plain read of the shape from the running line: closed late if the horse gained 2 or more lengths between the second call and the finish, faded late if it lost 2 or more, even shape otherwise. A fact about that one race, not a score. See "Worth a second look" above for where the shape is used.

Full Field columns

Form arrow — beaten-lengths trend across the last few starts, oldest to newest: green ▲ closing (finishing closer than before), red ▼ widening (falling further behind), dash flat. Tap the arrow to reveal the actual sequence. A display fact, same as pace.

Speed column with LONE tag — Quirin speed points, BRIS's own 0–8 scale for early-speed tendency, not a speed figure. LONE means the top horse is at least 5 on that scale and at least 2 points clear of the next — likely gets an uncontested early lead. The 8-point scale has nothing to do with field size.

The numeric speed column (e.g. "94 (88)") — the actual BRIS speed figure: last race, best figure in parentheses if different. This is the number the figure favourite rule is built on.

Tapping around

Any horse name with a dotted underline opens its full past performances. Inside that view, tap the horse's own name again to return to wherever you came from — Top 4, Full Field, a race card. Closing normally (the ✕ or tapping outside) does the same.
